summary: This note summarizes the 2016 Los Angeles Rams NFL season. The team sought to improve on its 7-9 record from 2015, started 3-1, then collapsed to finish 4-12, going 1-11 in its final 12 games. The Rams also missed the playoffs for the 12th straight season and clinched a 13th straight losing season, and they were the only team to lose to the 49ers that year.
one_line: The 2016 Los Angeles Rams season, in which a 3-1 start gave way to a 4-12 finish and continued playoff and losing-season streaks.
key_facts: The 2016 Los Angeles Rams season aimed to improve upon the team's 7-9 record from 2015.
The Rams started the 2016 season 3-1 before struggling in the second half.
The Rams went 1-11 in their final 12 games of the 2016 season.
The Los Angeles Rams finished the 2016 season with a 4-12 record.
The Rams went 1-7 at home in 2016, their worst home record since going 0-8 at home in their 1-15 2009 season.
The Los Angeles Rams missed the playoffs for the 12th straight season in 2016.
The Rams' playoff drought in 2016 was the 3rd longest current streak in the NFL, behind the Buffalo Bills and Cleveland Browns.
The Los Angeles Rams clinched their 13th straight losing season in 2016, the longest current such streak in the NFL.
The Los Angeles Rams were the only team to lose to the San Francisco 49ers in 2016.
Both of the San Francisco 49ers' wins in 2016 were against the Los Angeles Rams.
